BrainCodec is a high-fidelity quantized autoencoder neural compressor for EEG and iEEG signals.
BrainCodec can achieve compression ratios as high as 64x on both iEEG and EEG signals without significant loss in reconstruction quality.
Training BrainCodec on higher-quality iEEG data leads to better performance when compressing noisier EEG signals compared to training on EEG data directly.
The authors define high-fidelity reconstruction of EEG signals as having PRD lower than 30, less than 1% drop in downstream task performance, and high expert-rated quality.
BrainCodec outperforms classical and neural network-based EEG compression methods like NLSPIHT, AAC, and ANN in terms of both compression ratio and reconstruction fidelity.
The authors train and test BrainCodec on multiple iEEG datasets (SWEC, MC, Treebark) and EEG datasets (CHB-MIT, BONN, BCI IV-2a).
BrainCodec trained on iEEG data and used to compress EEG signals consistently achieves better performance at high compression ratios compared to BrainCodec trained on EEG.
Training BrainCodec on a mix of iEEG and EEG data improves its performance at compressing EEG signals compared to training on EEG alone.
The authors use a multi-scale STFT-based discriminator in BrainCodec to improve the reconstruction of high frequencies in the signals.
BrainCodec achieves reconstruction fidelity high enough to ensure no performance degradation on downstream seizure detection and motor imagery tasks.
